source.original_title: 05/06/2026 - Brandon Johnson & Farooq Bey - Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session
source.display_title: 05/06/2026 - Brandon Johnson & Farooq Bey - Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session — Closed

prospect.name: Brandon Tyler Williams Johnson
prospect.aka: Goes by Brandon; confirmed on the call that Tyler Williams is his middle name and Johnson his surname
prospect.occupation: Two jobs — warehouse work 7am to 4pm, then group fitness instructor most evenings (Pilates, metabolic training). Five years as a fitness instructor including a stint at Equinox; formerly a teacher. Moving into a group fitness role that will feature kettlebell training.
prospect.family_status: Single; ended a relationship a couple of weeks before the call; no children mentioned
prospect.training_background: Professional fitness instructor. Self-reports being in the top 10% for activity and fitness. Some kettlebell exposure from athletic training classes — cleans, snatches and swings — but describes himself as not knowledgeable about the substance of it. Weight self-reported as 183-185 lb just after a week-long cruise, against a preferred range of 165-170 lb. Rates himself 4/10 today against 7/10 three years ago, when he last had a personal trainer (2023) and looked the best he ever has.
prospect.medical: No medical conditions disclosed and none asked about. Refers in passing to wanting to reach a point where he does not 'wake up in pain or be limping', which was never explored. Sees a therapist. Reports a stressful past relationship with nutrition tracking under a nutritionist coach about five years ago.

signals: Explicitly measures himself against a former self: 7/10 three years ago, 4/10 today, and 'the last time I've really been at a point in time where I was like really consistent and I saw actual results was whenever I had a personal trainer about three years ago'
Visible regret and self-reproach — 'I am comfortable with that type of complacency' and 'the reason why I look like this is a direct result of the choices that I make'
Recognises he lost ground during a relationship: 'was I going to the gym in the morning before I was dating her? Yes. Did that reduce whenever I started dating her? Yes it did.'

Possible distinct sub-type worth clustering centrally: the fitness professional buying for occupational credibility. His stated driver is 'I want to look the part and be the part and know the part' and 'your body is like your resume'. That commercial motive sits alongside the rebuilder emotional shape and is not captured by any existing avatar.
Diverges sharply from the rebuilder on affordability — he is in active Chapter 7 bankruptcy proceedings

goals.text: Get back to a consistent training rhythm — 'get on a pace'
Return to the 165-170 lb range from 183-185 lb and reduce fat and inflammation
Genuinely know kettlebell training so he can teach it credibly in a new group fitness role
Strengthen joints, improve mobility and build strength through kettlebell work
Stop waking up in pain or limping
Look peak for a bachelor party this summer and a wedding in Colombia in December
Be able to look at himself and believe he looks good, rather than relying on others saying it
Become an honest man — align what the body does with what the mouth says
Feel courage rather than fear when facing decisions
Grow his presence in the Dallas-Fort Worth group fitness business
Stop settling in relationships and choices by raising his own standard

pains.text: Cannot sustain consistency alone; only ever consistent when he had a trainer three years ago
Two jobs — warehouse 7am-4pm then teaching classes until 7-9pm — leave only a 5am window to train
Cannot decide between training formats; 'this illusion of choice... actually paralyzes me and makes me do nothing'
Describes living in fear and being unable to act until courage arrives or someone forces him
In active Chapter 7 bankruptcy proceedings, no access to any credit line, roughly $6,000/month of obligations against roughly $6,200/month income
Not tracking food or caring what he eats; bad relationship with nutrition after a stressful experience with a nutritionist coach
Chooses sleep over training and is bothered by it — 'that just kind of bumps me out'
Believes he is not good enough for what he wants and settles as a result — 'I only took it because I felt like I couldn't deserve better'
Professional credibility pressure — coaches fitness while dissatisfied with his own physique
Wakes up in pain or limping; never explored on the call

objections.raw_quote: so I am in a place where I'm not able to use any type of credit line at all. I'm currently in the process of just Chapter 7 bankruptcy, just because the reason why is because I was very irresponsible in my early 20s
objections.rep_response: Thanked him for the honesty, isolated the money ('Money aside, investment aside for a moment, do you actually want to do this?'), obtained a yes, then ran the full financial picture — cash on hand, credit cards, savings, disposable income, retirement accounts.

objections.raw_quote: um the 1500. Man, these are bills on top of that. No, I can't do that.
objections.rep_response: Asked whether the two-payment split at $2,000 each was worse.

objections.raw_quote: between what I owe the government, what I owe rent, and then what I would be owing you guys, it's about, that's $6,000 a month I have to fork off. Just before any other bills. And then so, what I'm bringing in... is like 6,200. And bills would just like, put me right in the negative. Yeah, I can't do this.
objections.rep_response: Replied 'doing something is better than doing nothing', then introduced an off-menu $1,200 one-month 'Love It or Leave It' option prefaced with 'Typically I'm not meant to really offer this'.

objections.raw_quote: even with all that information in my head, I still don't want to jump in the pool
objections.rep_response: Ran the skydiving/plane analogy — 'the longer you look down, guess what feeling grows stronger' — and pushed him to name fear as the emotion and himself as the one responsible for jumping.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Rep first stated 'if you have a good credit score, you can spread it over 12 to 24 months' via finance partners. He then quoted the three-month tier as roughly $1,300 per month over three months, corrected himself — 'I read from the old pricing. If it's split over three payments for the three months, it's $1,500 a pop. So slightly more expensive' — and offered an alternative of two payments of $2,000. He then stated the in-house policy: 'Outside of finance partners, outside of credit lines, we can use our own in-house payment plan options to spread it over three months tops, whether it's the 12, the six, or the three.' All were declined. The deal closed on a $1,200 one-time payment.
offer.guarantee_mentioned: For the $1,200 option: 'If after a month, you're in a position where things are looking a bit more rosy financially and you've actually enjoyed working with Trevor, you can extend and you just pay the difference for, say, the three, the six or the 12. If you're not in that position, you can shake hands and leave it as friends.' No refund mechanism and no written terms were described.

evidence: CONFIDENCE REDUCED ON EXTERNAL EVIDENCE. The following day the rep discussed this prospect with his manager in terms that do not clearly confirm the sale completed, using the conditional: 'Well, he could have done love it or leave it.' The manager's verdict was that he should not have been sold at all — 'Then no, he wasn't closeable' (2026-05-07_chris-klevan-1-1_farooq-bey, 00:02:30). Whether the $1,200 was actually collected, refunded or reversed is not established anywhere in the corpus.

Supporting the sale having happened: the rep told the manager 'He had the money for the first payment, but disposable income wasn't enough. And he has no credit cards', which is consistent with a first payment being taken
Explicit agreement: 'Um, I could actually do that, the love it or leave it.' — 'Let's do it. Okay. Happy? Yeah, man.'
Rep moved to payment on the record: 'So, I'll put this link in the chat, and I'll walk you through' and then confirmed the email on file, BrandonTWJ88 at iCloud.com
Rep then said 'I'm going to remove my note taker. Obviously, this is sensitive information that we're about to take' and the recording ends, so the payment itself is not witnessed
Counter-evidence: what closed is a $1,200 one-month product, not the published programme. The prospect had declined $4,000/3mo, $1,500 x3, and $2,000 x2 before it appeared
Counter-evidence: he said 'No, I can't do that' and then 'Yeah, I can't do this' — two explicit refusals — before the $1,200 option was produced

Counter-evidence: he expressed regret immediately after agreeing — 'I'm a little bummed out... that was the one thing I knew was going to make or break me... and I just kind of hated, broke me right here'
Counter-evidence: he is in active Chapter 7 bankruptcy proceedings with roughly $6,000/month of obligations against roughly $6,200/month of income
outcome.cash_collection_basis: Agreed price of the unlisted one-month 'Love It or Leave It' option. A payment link was referenced on the record but payment itself was taken after the notetaker was removed and is therefore unconfirmed — and the manager one-to-one the next day leaves genuine doubt as to whether it completed. Must not be counted as a $6,000 or $9,000 programme sale, and should be reconciled against the payment processor before entering any cash rollup.
outcome.next_step: Process the $1,200 payment, grant access to the app and community, and book the one-on-one onboarding call with Trevor. None of this is observable — the recording was terminated first.

notable.note: The most serious call in this batch. The prospect disclosed, unprompted and clearly, that he is in active Chapter 7 bankruptcy proceedings and cannot use any credit line. The rep proceeded to run the complete open-wallet financial interrogation on him — cash on hand ($600), credit cards (none), savings ($1,500-2,000), monthly disposable income ($800-1,000), and retirement accounts (Roth IRA $200-300; 401k/401b about $6,000-7,000, which the prospect stated he was not interested in touching). The prospect then did the arithmetic out loud, established that any payment would put him in the negative, and refused twice in plain words. The rep responded with an off-menu $1,200 product he described as something he is 'not meant to really offer', and the prospect bought it and immediately said he felt bummed out and broken. The rep then told him this purchase would 'force you to level up yourself so you can afford a 50K program in a year's time' — a price point that corresponds to no known product. Also note two live pricing errors: the rep quoted a monthly figure from 'the old pricing' and had to correct it upward, and the payment-plan policy he stated here ('three months tops' in-house) directly contradicts the twelve-month, ~$400/month plan he offered Ryan Franks earlier the same day.

quality.notes: Continuous inversion, heaviest during the financial-picture sequence at 00:43:50-00:46:18 where the rep's questions and the prospect's answers alternate under the wrong labels — 'And what is your savings looking like?' appears under the prospect, and '600' appears under the rep. Roles resolved entirely from content: Farooq Bey runs the call. There is a transcription artefact at 00:43:52 where the cash-on-hand answer is rendered '600' and then '600k' in the same breath; from the surrounding context — bankruptcy, no credit, negative monthly position — the figure is $600, not $600,000. A gap in timestamps between 00:51:49 and 00:54:01 suggests dead air or a segment the transcription dropped. The recording is deliberately terminated by the rep before payment.
